parsed.explanation: Combined regime is High Risk. Federal passport sex-marker restrictions are in effect, and entry officers are instructed to refuse discrepant applicants and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility. The division's criminal bathroom law from 1 July 2026 reaches public-facing private businesses with up to a year in jail. A documented arrest under a comparable law held a trans woman 24 hours in a men's ward. Federal immigration custody shows documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Counterterrorism framing names 'radically pro-transgender' groups. No capital or lethal pathway is documented, and the division's injunction status and the federal litigation remain unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports cannot carry a marker differing from sex at birth; the 24 Feb 2025 cable directs refusal of discrepant applicants and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Passports have been confiscated or blocked, leaving some stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid to expiry; the fraud ground needs all four elements and is never automatic; litigation is pending.
entry_documents.interaction: A home-issued credential can conflict with the passport; a division X-marker ID does not cure a federal passport mismatch at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Division bathroom trespass arrest (first known, 19 Mar 2025) with handcuffing and 24h hold in a men's ward. Federal immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave when asked; release on pretrial release occurred.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Bathroom enforcement by building staff can move a visitor into police custody and birth-sex placement, then into federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in 19 state/provinces cover government buildings and schools; 6 reach some private settings. The division criminalises use of non-matching facilities in government buildings and public-facing private businesses, with steeper penalties than peers. Federal corrections adopted conversion-type policies, including hormone removal.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division's statute has an exemption list (chaperoning, emergencies, custodial purposes). 29 state/provinces and the capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal rules and division criminal law operate together, so a traveller meets both exposures in one stay; the division's X ID option does not exempt facility use.

care_services.exposure: Federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19s; proposed rules to bar public insurance for under-18s; prison hormone removal. Care for minors is banned in 27 state/provinces; the division's 2019 health board rule removed doctor approval for minors.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not restricted in the sources; a 2024 ruling allows hormones in state prisons; federal rules are unfinalised.
care_services.interaction: Records requested by federal agencies can expose a visitor's care history, and a care-seeker can become an investigated subject.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dec 2025 reward system and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy target 'radically pro-transgender' groups; federal guidance lists 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist markers; a federal memo directs prosecution of teachers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy says it will not target people who merely disagree with it.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing by federal law enforcement can make a visitor's advocacy or association visible to security services.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division parental-disclosure law (Mar 2026) requires schools, childcare and medical staff to tell parents within 3 days. Federal teacher-prosecution directive. Travelling with a minor for care is exposed to minors' care bans and records demands. The 2022 bill penalising parents who took children out of state for care was blocked.
minors_guardians.protection: The parental-travel felony bill was blocked; a 2020 sports ban applies to teams, not visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Disclosure duties and border questioning can reveal a minor's status to a guardian or an official.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence above the general homicide baseline is documented. Bias against sexual orientation is a large share of single-bias hate incidents, a general pattern not trans-specific.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute applies; 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes; 37 lacked such statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Gaps in state bias statutes leave recourse uneven; police involvement in bathroom enforcement can itself create exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division litigation status and any 16 June 2026 narrowing are unsourced. No enforcement against a visitor under the division measure is recorded. Federal orders are partly enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-rights suits are pending; 22 state/provinces plus the capital district bar gender-identity discrimination; municipal ordinances cover about 40% of the population.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Injunctions may change which rules apply during a visit; a traveller cannot predict which measures are operative at the time of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both have criminal exposure for presentation and custody assault, but 0.15-E has prison assaults, capital ambiguity and monitors denied entry. This dossier has no documented capital pathway, and its custody harm sits in federal immigration detention, not a broader prison system. It sits clearly higher.
Similar: a birth-sex document rule, raids or arrests, fines and settlements. The dossier adds documented sexual abuse in immigration custody and a lifetime fraud ground, so it is somewhat lower.

0.35-A is a universal entry bar with exclusion and no arrest. This dossier adds a criminal bathroom statute with jail, documented arrest, and custody harm, so it sits lower. It is comparable on passport and entry refusal.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets stacked exposures: passport marker mismatch with refusal and confiscation at entry, a division criminal bathroom law reaching private businesses with jail exposure, and federal and state birth-sex facility rules. Any mismatch in a facility or check can move the visitor into a 24-hour men's-ward hold or birth-sex custody. Documented custody abuse in federal immigration detention adds severity. Mitigations are real but unevidenced in operation: pending suits, possible injunctions, and anti-discrimination coverage in 22 jurisdictions. No capital or lethal pathway is documented. The result is high risk rather than severe.
